purpose: Test South Asian and transregional Buddhist philosophical structures against current Factorium owners while preserving every source-local factoring for GPC-09.

packet_slots.position: Upaniṣadic debates about self, ultimate reality, knowledge, and liberation
Advaita and rival Vedānta analyses of self, reality, difference, and liberation
Sāṃkhya-Yoga analyses of consciousness, nature, causation, discipline, and discernment
Nyāya analyses of knowledge sources, inference, testimony, debate, and error
Mīmāṃsā analyses of language, testimony, action, duty, and interpretation
Jaina analyses of nonviolence, many-sidedness, standpoint, substance, change, and liberation
Cārvāka and related naturalist or materialist limits on knowledge, self, and afterlife
Sikh analyses of selfhood, ego, truthful living, service, justice, and liberation
Early Buddhist analyses of suffering, craving, impermanence, no-self, and dependent arising
Abhidharma analyses of events, aggregates, causal conditions, mind, and person-construction
Madhyamaka analyses of emptiness, intrinsic nature, dependence, and two truths
Yogācāra analyses of consciousness, three natures, representation, and transformation
Dignāga-Dharmakīrti analyses of perception, inference, exclusion, and reliable cognition
Tibetan scholastic analyses of debate, path, conventional truth, and competing Madhyamaka interpretations
Chinese Tiantai and Huayan analyses of interdependence, part-whole relation, and multiple truths
Chan and Zen analyses of practice, language, direct experience, and awakening
Pure Land analyses of faith, practice, other-power, aspiration, and liberation
Theravāda and Southeast Asian analyses of mind, ethics, insight, and liberation

selection_rules: A slot is a disputed position-space, not a claim that its label names one uniform school.
Each slot requires at least one established specialist source and visible internal or external alternatives.
Primary-text language and established translations are retained when available; English glosses remain working mappings.
A slot may split before execution when source review shows that its present scope would erase a governing distinction.
No slot may be dropped solely because it yields no mapping or conflicts with another slot.
stop: Complete the frozen slots once, retain splits and nulls, and hand only source-local records plus typed alignment candidates to later boundary design and GPC-09.
